test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A tower stands vertically on the ground. From point P, which is located 40 meters from the ground at the base of the tower, the angle of elevation to the tower's top is α, where tan(α) equals 1.5. From another point Q, situated 60 meters away from the foot of the tower (in line with point P and the tower's base), the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is β. What is the value of tan(β)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Tower Height (H) = distanceP × tan(α)

H = 40 × 1.5 = 60 m

tan(β) = Height ÷ distanceQ

tan(β) = 60 ÷ 60 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of point P from the foot of the tower (dP) = 40 m

Angle of elevation at P = α, where tan(α) = 1.5

Distance of point Q from the foot of the tower (dQ) = 60 m

Angle of elevation at Q = β

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/838f8fd309b4c028ffb28e47f5d2868069dad5f05adb62368a8cc82094007584.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base (Distance)

**Calculations:**

In triangle formed by the tower and point P:

⇒ tan(α) = Height ÷ DistanceP

⇒ 1.5 = Height ÷ 40

⇒ Height = 1.5 × 40

⇒ Height = 60 m

Now, in triangle formed by the tower and point Q:

⇒ tan(β) = Height ÷ DistanceQ

⇒ tan(β) = 60 ÷ 60

⇒ tan(β) = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. tan(θ) = Height ÷ Distance.

Trigonometric Ratios

For standard angles: tan(30°) = 1/√3, tan(45°) = 1, tan(60°) = √3. If tan(β) = 1, then β = 45°.

Relationship of Distances

For a constant height, the tangent of the angle of elevation is inversely proportional to the horizontal distance from the base: tan(α) × d₁ = tan(β) × d₂.
